packages.title: Airports
packages.desc: 3,214 airports and 18,858 routes. Hubs, communities, shortest paths and what happens when airports close.
packages.page: Network theory, told with the world's airports
packages.sub: told with the world's airports
packages.aria: Interactive globe of the world airline network

packages.title: The future
packages.desc: A 3D tour of the Ludwig Boltzmann Institute for Network Medicine: protein machines, the interactome as a map, rare diseases, organs and tissues.
packages.page: A glimpse into the future of network medicine
packages.sub: a glimpse into the future
packages.aria: Interactive 3D tour of network medicine, from proteins to the whole body

packages.title: Muscle and heart
packages.desc: Rare diseases of nerves and muscles in a 71-layer network: a random walk, disease modules, endotypes, and what muscle and heart share.
packages.page: Rare muscle diseases, seen through 71 layers
packages.sub: rare diseases in 71 layers
packages.aria: Interactive 3D multiplex network of rare neuromuscular diseases

packages.title: Endotypes
packages.desc: A group of rare diseases of the junction between nerve and muscle, 35 genes and 12 endotypes: how a random walk and a tree that splits only when the data say so find them.
packages.page: Endotypes: one disease, many mechanisms
packages.sub: one disease, many mechanisms
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how disease endotypes are found, from a nerve-muscle junction to a protein network

packages.title: One scan, one system
packages.desc: A PET scan sees every organ's sugar use at once. 658 scans make a network of organs that thins and tips towards a few hubs as health erodes; the aim is to read one scan against such a network.
packages.page: One scan, one system: the body as a metabolic network
packages.sub: the body as a metabolic network
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of whole-body PET scans and the network of the organs' metabolism

packages.title: Tissue and time
packages.desc: Organs are built from small working units of cells. 24,945 slides of 40 tissues show which ones there are, how they connect, and which change as we age.
packages.page: Tissue and time: how organs are built, and how they age
packages.sub: how organs are built, and how they age
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of the microanatomy of human tissues and how it changes with age

packages.title: The aging ovary
packages.desc: Sections of 255 ovaries from donors aged 20 to 70, read by deep learning: follicles run out, scars pile up and blood vessels grow fewer. Two methods, one picture of aging.
packages.page: The aging ovary: what 255 ovaries show about aging
packages.sub: what 255 ovaries show about aging
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how the human ovary changes with age, seen through deep learning on 255 tissue sections

packages.title: Three qubits
packages.desc: Some diseases need two genes broken at once. To search the pairs on a quantum computer, a gene network is cut down to eight cells on three qubits, and its moves into a few building blocks.
packages.page: Three qubits: how a gene network fits on a tiny quantum computer
packages.sub: a gene network on a tiny quantum computer
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how a gene network is shrunk onto three qubits and broken into building blocks a quantum computer runs

packages.title: The mutation machine
packages.desc: DNA changes letter by letter as it is copied. A rule for those changes becomes a machine of gears on a quantum computer, one per branch of a family tree, and pairs of letters that change together are coupled.
packages.page: The mutation machine: DNA's changes as a quantum circuit
packages.sub: DNA's changes as a quantum circuit
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how DNA letters change along a family tree and how a quantum circuit models it, from a rule of change to an RNA stem

packages.title: The shape of tissue
packages.desc: Where cells sit in a slide of liver, read at every scale at once: balls grow round the cells, pieces join and loops open and close. From 123 slides, a classifier learns which scales tell cirrhosis from healthy tissue, and maps it back onto every cell.
packages.page: The shape of tissue: topology of cells in the liver
packages.sub: Topology of cells in the liver
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how the arrangement of cells in liver tissue is read at every scale with persistent homology, and how it tells cirrhosis from healthy tissue

packages.title: Pass it on
packages.desc: A school of fish, the world's flights and a cell: how a warning, an infection and a signal pass from neighbour to neighbour. In English and German.
packages.page: Pass it on: how warnings, viruses and signals spread
packages.sub: how warnings, viruses and signals spread
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how warnings, viruses and signals spread through networks: a school of fish, the airline network and a cell

packages.title: Holding on to nitrogen
packages.desc: Less than half of the fertiliser a farmer spreads ends up in the crop. In a field trial in Japan, a wheat with a trait from a wild grass stays greener and leaks less nitrate, while the soil's microbes follow the fertiliser far more than the wheat.
packages.page: Holding on to nitrogen: a wheat, its soil and the microbes in between
packages.sub: a wheat, its soil and its microbes
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of how soil microbes turn fertiliser into nitrate and nitrous oxide, a wheat bred to slow them down, and the network of microbes in a field trial

packages.title: The switch that sticks
packages.desc: CDK5 is a messenger in nerve cells that only works with a partner. Among 16,376 human proteins, meet its partners, listen in on three of its healthy conversations, see the cut that leaves it stuck on, as in Alzheimer's disease, and the landscape of diseases it points to; with real protein structures at the centre.
packages.page: The switch that sticks: CDK5, its network and brain diseases
packages.sub: CDK5, its network and brain diseases
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of the kinase CDK5 among the human interactome: its activators, its partners, three healthy pathways, how calpain cuts p35 and leaves CDK5 stuck on, its pathway in Alzheimer's disease and the diseases its network points to, with protein structures
packages.authors: Christiane Hütter (the Menche lab's CDK5_data); structures from the Protein Data Bank; the app's authors

packages.title: Proteins
packages.desc: 254 proteins inside a human cell. Essential hubs, disease modules, drug targets and knockouts.
packages.page: Network medicine, told with the proteins in a cell
packages.sub: told with the proteins in a cell
packages.aria: Interactive 3D cell of protein interactions

packages.title: Cell map
packages.desc: 249 proteins in the compartments of a model cell. Proteins that move, signals that cross the cell, proteins in the wrong place.
packages.page: Spatial interactome, where proteins meet in a cell
packages.sub: where proteins meet in a cell
packages.aria: Interactive 3D model of a human cell and its protein network

packages.title: Back into the cell
packages.desc: An interactome of 13,460 proteins put back into a cell: which of its links can happen where, and why it is so hard to tell.
packages.page: Back into the cell: an interactome in a model cell
packages.sub: an interactome in a model cell
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story: an interactome put back into a model cell
packages.loading: Putting the proteins back into the cell
packages.authors: Jörg Menche and colleagues (the interactome); the Human Protein Atlas (the locations); the app's authors

packages.title: Flock
packages.desc: 200 starlings at dusk, flying all around you. Each follows its seven nearest neighbours: a network that never stands still.
packages.page: A flock of starlings, all around you
packages.sub: starlings at dusk
packages.aria: Interactive 3D flock of starlings flying around you at dusk

packages.title: Robot gang
packages.desc: A gang of robot vacuums in your room. In a headset they find your floor and walls, follow you about and bounce off the walls.
packages.page: A gang of robot vacuums in your room
packages.sub: vacuums in your room
packages.aria: Interactive 3D room with a gang of robot vacuums that follow you about

packages.title: Your guide
packages.desc: A robot guide shows you how the app works in a headset: pointing, playing a story, exploring, the menu and shared rooms. Then a few tasks to practise.
packages.page: Tutorial: a robot guide shows you round
packages.sub: a robot guide shows you round
packages.aria: Interactive 3D tutorial in which a robot guide shows how to use the app in a headset

packages.title: Cell stress test
packages.desc: The cell map's model cell filled with up to 20,000 made-up proteins and 80,000 links, to read a headset's frame rate at each size.
packages.aria: Interactive 3D test: the cell map's model cell with many made-up proteins and links

packages.title: Invisible threads
packages.desc: Nearly ten thousand substances from air, water, food and medicines, tied together by the genes they disturb: what they do in our cells, which diseases sit close by, and what Europe's releases may mean.
packages.page: Invisible threads: the chemicals around us and the diseases they touch
packages.sub: the chemicals around us and the diseases they touch
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story of the chemical exposome: about ten thousand substances linked by the genes they disturb, their groups, where they hit the cell's network of proteins, the diseases close to them and the substances released in European countries
packages.authors: Lombardo, Hütter, Unterlass and Menche (the map and its data); the app's authors

packages.title: Six handshakes
packages.desc: Sixty people in a ring, and how a few shortcuts bring everyone close: the example story package.
packages.aria: Interactive 3D story: Six handshakes, small-world networks
